newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - TAT/Air Liberte strike imperils recovery.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - TAT/Air Liberte strike imperils recovery.

text.p: A cockpit crew strike at British Airways' French carriers TAT and Air Liberte puts their recovery at risk, the sales director of TAT-Air Liberte said on Wednesday.

If the eight-day strike goes on, it "could put the recovery objectives at risk although I think the situation's salvageable if everyone gets back to work," Bernard Lalanne told Reuters in an interview.

"Since January 9, the date of the takeover (of Air Liberte by British Airways), we were on track for a recovery. The monthly results were even better than our targets. For the moment, we're at a dead halt," Lalanne said.
Unions said on Wednesday they would pursue the strike for a ninth day on Thursday to protest against cost-cutting plans.
The management has called a staff council meeting for Friday to discuss the condition of TAT and Air Liberte, which were brought under joint management on April 1.
BA's objective is to bring the two airlines to breakeven by 1998. They lost 1.2 billion francs last year -- Air Liberte lost around one billion francs, and TAT lost 200 million.

The recovery plan entails sharp reductions in costs, including a proposed 15 percent cut in the wages of pilots and flight engineers, leading to the labour conflict. The company has been able to ensure only 40 percent of scheduled flights.

The conflicts have grown since the two carriers were brought under joint management as their wage scales differ. Wages at TAT are generally higher than those at Air Liberte even though TAT pilots and flight engineers took a 15 percent cut in 1996.
The unions say the company's objective is to standardize wages on the lowest scale.
"It's clear there are big gaps between cockpit crew wages at Air Liberte and TAT. We want to bring TAT's staff in a zone closer to Air Liberte," Lalanne said.
He said the management was open to negotiation on certain issues, such as the 13th month wage traditionally paid in France, rest rules and wages for contract employees.
But, he added, "TAT-Air Liberte's costs have to be competitive within the new deregulated European framework. Many airlines will be threatened if they can't operate with lower costs."
